ai_explanation.concept_rule: The area between two intersecting curves is obtained by finding the intersection points and integrating the difference $(\text{upper curve} - \text{lower curve})$ over each interval.
step_by_step: Set the equations equal to each other to determine the $x$-coordinates of intersection.
Identify which function is on top over each interval between consecutive intersection points.
Set up the definite integrals with appropriate order of subtraction.
Integrate and apply the fundamental theorem of calculus to find the total area.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Failing to split the integral at $x = 0$, leading to negative areas canceling out positive areas.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: To find the area between two curves, solve for points of intersection, determine the orientation of the curves across each sub-interval, and integrate the upper minus the lower curve over each interval.
step_by_step: Solve $x^3 - 2x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$ to find the intersection points $x = -2, 1, 3$.
Identify which curve is higher in each interval: on $[-2, 1]$, $2x^3-5x+4$ is above; on $[1, 3]$, $x^3+2x^2-2$ is above.
Set up the sum of two definite integrals.
Find antiderivatives and substitute the limits accurately.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Arithmetic errors when expanding and simplifying polynomial powers and negative fractions.
